newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania raises fuel prices by up to 29 percent.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania raises fuel prices by up to 29 percent.

text.p: The state-owned Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation ordered increases in fuel prices from Saturday of up to 29 percent, the first rises in two years.

"There has been a price increase today but it's largely a reflection of rising crude oil and product prices in world markets...It's the first rise in Tanzania in two years," said Stuart Johnson, Managing Director of British Petroleum Tanzania.

The increases applied to petrol, oil, kerosene, cooking gas, jet fuel, diesel and furnace oil. Jet fuel for instance rose 15.9 percent from 170 shillings per litre to 220 while diesel was up 29.4 percent from 283 shillings a litre to 328 shillings. ($1=598 Tanzanian shillings)
